senses.gloss:
dreams
------------------------------------------
‘Snakes’ and द्रेअम्स् have come in very handy for the Advaita Vedānta philosophy to prove one of its cardinal teachings viz., the unreality of this world. If the ‘snake’ in the rajju-sarpa-न्याय (the maxim of the rope appearing as a snake in insufficient light) serves as the proof for the absolute unreality of this world, the dream can help in proving its relative reality. Just as a dream is real as long as it lasts, this world too is real as long as we are under the sway of अविद्या or nescience.
However, द्रेअम्स् assume a much greater significance in other fields of knowledge like आयुर्वेद (health-science) and prognostication or futurology. Directions have also been given in them as to how to utilise them to one’s advantage if they predict good things and how to offset them if they forebode evil.
Dreams can be caused by physical causes like the disturbance of the हुमोउर्स् (kapha or phlegm, vāta or wind and pitta or bile), past experiences of this life or the past lives. Depending upon the type and the time of occurrence of the द्रेअम्स्, the results are predicated. द्रेअम्स् occurring in the first part of the night will give their results in one year, in the second part in eight months, in the third part in three months and at dawn, in 10 days. The result may be immediate if the person wakes up at once.
If the person sleeps again after the dream or tells others about it, the dream will not give its results.
Seeing the following in a dream is considered as auspicious: elephant, a king, gold, a bull, a cow, a lighted lamp, ड़ोओद्, fruits, a maiden, an umbrella, a chariot and a flag.
The following objects seen in a dream forebode evil: shaving of the head, nakedness, wearing dirty garments, falling from high spots like a hill, riding boars, asses and camels, killing horses, ascending a funeral pyre, falling of sun and मोओन्, playing with goblins, plunging into oil or drinks, wearing red garments or applying red unguents and so on.
The epics and the पुराणस् contain innumerable verses on this subject.
The remedies suggested to offset the effects of bad द्रेअम्स् are: performing a śrāddha like the one on an अमावास्या day or reciting holy texts like the Durgā-saptaśatī or the Viṣṇusahasranāma or the Gajendramokṣa part of the Bhāgavata. Performance of appropriate शान्तिस् (reli-gious rites to bring about auspicious results) is also recommended.
The work Adbhutasāgara of the king Ballaḷasena of Bengal (A. D. 1168) is considered as a great authority on this subject.

dreṣkāṇa
(also spelt as drekkāṇa)
------------------------------------------
Jyautiṣa or the ‘science of light’ is an ancient science, the science of astro-nomy and अस्त्रोलोग्य् combined. Out of the several technical words used in Hindu अस्त्रोलोग्य्, the word ‘dreṣkāṇa’ (or drekkāṇa) is also one.
When a sign of the zodiac is divided into three equal parts, each part is called ‘dreṣkāṇa’. The lord of the first द्रेष्काण is the owner of the sign itself. The lord of the second द्रेष्काण is the lord of the 5th sign in question. The lord of the third द्रेष्काण is the lord of the 9th sign.
For instance, consider the zodiacal sign Meṣa or Aries. Divide it into three equal parts, each being called a द्रेष्काण. The first is governed by the sign of Meṣa or Aries, viz., कुज or Mars. The second is ruled by the lord of the 5th sign (Siṁha or Leo), viz., Ravi or Sun. The third is ruled by the lord of the 9th (Śani or Sagittarius), viz., गुरु or जुपितेर्.
The ecliptic (of 360°) is divided into 12 Rāśis or ज़ोदिअचल् सिग्न्स् like Meṣa (Aries), Vṛṣabha (Taurus) and so on, each occupying 30° in the same. It is this 30° that is divided into 3 dreṣkāṇas, each द्रेष्काण being of 10° extension.
The word द्रेष्काण is said to be of Egyptian or Greek origin, the original word being ‘decanoi’ (deca = 10). Each of these 36 had its own geni or deity, ruling over it.
These terms and associated ideas have their own use in astrological calculations.
